programs.name: Paraplegic Veterans Property Tax Exemption

summary.correct: Full exemption of a dwelling (designed for wheelchair use per 10-4-24.9) owned and occupied for the full calendar year by a paraplegic veteran or a veteran with loss or loss of use of both lower extremities, or the unremarried widow/widower. Discretionary county refund up to four prior years.
summary.quote: A dwelling or part of a dwelling designed as provided in § 10-4-24.9 that is owned and occupied for the full calendar year in which a tax is to be levied by a paraplegic veteran, a veteran with the loss or loss of use of both lower extremities, or the unremarried widow or widower of the veteran is exempt from taxation.

survivingSpouse.quote: or the unremarried widow or widower of the veteran is exempt from taxation

programs.effectiveChanges: SL 2026 ch 39 (effective 7/1/2026) added the four-year discretionary refund petition for missed deadlines; no dollar change.
programs.note: Condition-based (paraplegia / bilateral lower-extremity loss), not rating-based; ratingRequired null is right but the tool should gate it on the condition, not credit it to every 100% veteran.

programs.name: Disabled Veterans Property Tax Exemption

exemptionValue.quote: Two hundred thousand dollars of the full and true value of the total amount of a dwelling or portion thereof classified as owner-occupied ... which is owned and occupied by a veteran who is rated as permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability, is exempt from property taxation.
exemptionValue.note: Confirmed in the codified text as amended by SL 2026 ch 40 (HB 1193 enrolled keeps $200,000). The $225,000 figure circulating online was HB 1241 (2026), which did not become law. 'Full and true value' = market value, not assessed value.

survivingSpouse.quote: Two hundred thousand dollars of the full and true value ... is exempt from property taxation if owned and occupied by: (1) The surviving spouse of a veteran who was rated as permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability; or (2) The surviving spouse of a veteran, who receives dependency and indemnity compensation
survivingSpouse.note: Resolves the brief's lead: the spouse amount is $200,000 (not $150,000) and ends on remarriage.

ptRequired.quote: rated as permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability

programs.effectiveChanges: SL 2026 ch 40 (HB 1193, effective 7/1/2026): when the Nov 1 deadline is missed because of a pending VA P&T claim, the county 'must abate or refund the difference in taxes accumulated since the effective date of the claim, but not exceeding the previous four years.' No change to the $200,000 amount for TY2026/TY2027.
programs.note: Row otherwise correct. Summary text is accurate (apply by Nov 1 with the director of equalization).
